title: Console: Minimal cost+trace surface — compact route cards, conditional trace sampling, CSV export
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The full Console insights surface includes detailed route-level pivoting, per-request CSV exports, deep trace timeline controls and a historical cost heatmap. Given deadline and cost constraints we need a tightly constrained MVP that still gives customers actional cost and reliability signals for production inference workloads.

This ticket defines the pragmatic scope cuts, required acceptance criteria, and the rollforward/rollback plan that allow us to ship a compact observability surface with predictable unit-cost while leaving a clear path to restore cut features in later sprints. The goal is to maximize signal-per-work and keep engineering work focused on a small set of deliverables that address the most common support and billing questions customers raise.
scope_inclusions: Top-5 route compact cards showing: 7d cost delta, average latency, error rate, request throughput
Cost breakdown CSV export of displayed routes (server-side aggregation to keep UI light)
Trace sampling restricted to: error traces + slow traces (p95 > threshold) with a cap of 100 traces/day per customer
Lightweight route-level links to the logs/trace viewer (deep link only, no embedded timeline controls)
Backend aggregated endpoints to compute per-route totals with 24h resolution for the 7d view
scope_exclusions: Interactive pivot UI for arbitrary time windows and ad-hoc group-bys (deferred)
Per-token cost heatmaps and per-request token timelines (deferred)
Full tracing timeline with zoom/step controls embedded in the insight cards
Custom filter builder for cost dimensions (deferred)
Historical raw event retention > 30 days for the MVP metrics endpoints
acceptance_criteria: Compact dashboard renders within 700ms TTFB for users in US region on canary with production-like traffic
CSV export completes within 10s for top-5 route payloads under typical dataset sizes (validated in staging)
Trace intake rule only stores error and p95+ slow traces and never exceeds 100 traces/day/customer in repeated load tests
Observability product tests show route-level cost totals within +/-3% of billing system for sampled customers
Feature flags exist for: full-trace-ui, expanded-pivot, csv-export and are off by default; canary rollout to 2% orgs
UI provides clear empty-state copy that explains missing features and links to roadmap for restored capabilities
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers expect the full pivoting experience and will raise support tickets. Mitigation: Provide clear copy and a short survey link in the UI and prepare canned messaging for support
Risk: Cost aggregation drift vs billing system. Mitigation: Run reconciliation job daily during rollout and surface delta dashboard; if drift >5% pause rollout
Risk: Traces cap may drop important samples. Mitigation: Use dynamic thresholding (tighten p95 threshold only after canary) and allow SRE emergency override per-org
Risk: Unknown perf regressions under concurrency. Mitigation: Include throughput and load tests with production-like concurrency before 2% canary
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Feature flag QA in staging + perf/load tests (owner: ENG-observability)
Phase 1 - Internal-only dogfood for 72 hours, collect deltas and UX notes
Phase 2 - 2% canary to production via flag, monitor cost-delta, CSV latency, trace caps for 48 hours
Phase 3 - 25% ramp if metrics stable, continue to 100% within one week if no regressions
Rollback criteria: cost-delta >5%, CSV error rate >1%, user-visible latency >2x baseline — disable flags and notify customers
decisions: Cut interactive pivoting (deferred) to reduce frontend complexity and telemetry costs
Provide CSV export instead of in-UI pivoting to cover immediate billing reconciliation needs
Limit trace sampling to errors + slow traces to reduce storage and privacy surface while keeping high-value signals
